title: Surge absorber: SKU rotation & acquisition pipeline
content:
Purpose:
This working sheet defines a short-to-mid horizon plan for maintaining an operational spare pool across regions via staggered acquisitions and SKU rotations. Goal is to keep 10–25% usable spare capacity per region under normal burn, and a documented surge-absorber lane for 30–90 day spikes without emergency rentals.

Scope:
- Regional scope: us-west-2, us-east-1, eu-west-1, ap-south-1
- SKUs covered: H100-80GB, A100-80GB, L4x, rented short-term blades (vendor pool)
- Time horizon: next 180 days (quarterly cadence)

Summary (quick take):
- Current cross-region on-hand usable GPUs: 4,850 devices (includes reserve pool and RMAs)
- In-transit / ordered (confirmed POs): 1,420 devices with broad ETAs (range below)
- Allocation to customers / Dedicated: 3,900 devices (net usable = on-hand + in-transit - allocated = 2,370)
- Target spare ratio (operational): 15% baseline, 22% preferred for high-risk regions (eu, apac)

Key metrics table (csv-like):

Runway calc examples (operational):
- Daily burn (global) = 18.3 devices/day (production token-weighted); regional burn scaled by customer commit.
- Days of runway (eu-west-1 H100) = (on_hand + in_transit - allocated) / regional_daily_burn.
  Example: (600 + 320 - 400) / 5.2 ≈ 100 days.

Acquisition cadence and ETA bands (active orders):
- P-2301-H100-USW: 400 H100; vendor confirms ship window 2024-02-15 -> 2024-03-30 (customs risk: medium).
- P-2319-A100-EU: 320 A100; ship window 2024-03-10 -> 2024-04-25 (lead-time sensitivity: port congest.)
- P-2324-L4-AP: 80 L4x; expedited air freight ETA 2024-02-28 (low customs risk).
- Short-term rental contracts: R-24Q1-01 vendor pool activated +370 devices available within 7–10 days of request.

Rotation logic (how we swap/rotate SKUs between regions):
1) Weekly review of burn and allocations; flag any region with projected runway < 45 days.
2) If flagged: attempt local rotation from nearest region with runway > 120 days (shipping by ocean/air depending on urgency).
3) If cross-region rotation cost > 30% of spot-rental monthly rate, prefer rental.
4) Preserve a minimum of 20% of in-region on-hand as non-rotatable for SLA-critical customers.

Reorder triggers (actionable SLOs):
- Green: runway > 90 days -> monitor.
- Amber: runway 45–90 days -> raise PO candidate and prepare cross-dock manifest.
- Red: runway < 45 days -> create immediate rental request + prioritized PO (expedite shipping) + open EO-ticket JIRA-INFRA-URG-1.

Lead-time sensitivity & customs slack assumptions:
- Typical factory lead -> ship: 45–90 calendar days (H100/A100), variable per vendor.
- Port + customs: 10–30 days depending on region and HS classification.
- Air freight (expensive): 3–10 days.
- Use transit slack multiplier of 1.25 for eu-west-1 and ap-south-1 when calculating ETA windows during Q1/Q2 peak.

Risk register (topline):
- Component shortage (memory modules) -> hold 2% of orders as refundable buffer (ask vendors for flexible cancellation window).
- Customs holdups -> prefer pre-cleared manifest for eu and apac lanes for highest priority orders.
- Sudden demand spike (customer onboarding wave) -> rental pool + cloud-burst fallback.
- Warranty RMA backlog -> maintain hot-swap pool of 120 devices globally.

Cost levers and rules of thumb:
- Cross-region shipping threshold: shift only when moved-device-cost < expected lost-revenue-per-device * 14 days.
- Rental vs buy heuristic: if spike expected < 90 days, prefer rental; if > 90 days, prefer purchase even if lead-time long.
- Batch consolidation: consolidate small orders into monthly LCL shipments for cost savings when not urgent.

Operational checklist (immediate next 30 days):
- [ ] Confirm P-2301-H100-USW customs pre-clearance (owner: Lucas Rivera) due 2024-02-05 (ticket: JIRA-INFRA-412).
- [ ] Validate rental pool readiness and ramp activation steps (owner: Priya Nair) due 2024-02-01.
- [ ] Run rotation simulation for eu-west -> us-east lane with 3 different burn scenarios and attach CSV outputs to Confluence (owner: Maya Desai) due 2024-02-08.
- [ ] Negotiate flexible cancellation windows with vendor X for tranche P-2320 (owner: Omar Haddad) due 2024-02-12.

Notes / open questions (working):
- Should we increase eu-west target_spare to 25% for GDPR-sensitive customer onboarding planned in Q2? (impact on cash & lead-time).
- Can vendors commit to shorter lead-time windows for partial shipments? We should push for split-shipment terms.
- Is there appetite from finance for larger refundable deposits to improve priority in vendor queues?
